extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. Unlike existing benchmarks, MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MMMU dataset was meticulously curated through a three-stage process. First, common university majors were reviewed to select subjects based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects to provide valuable information. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concerns of foundation models, the annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks. This process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data for MMMU was sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources. Annotators were instructed to avoid data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution and to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process was conducted over several months, with the final dataset compiled by June 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset underwent two steps of data cleaning. First, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involved distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step required authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations were found. The third and final stage involved categorizing the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was preprocessed to ensure consistency and quality. This included standardizing the format of questions and answers, categorizing questions by difficulty, and ensuring that all questions met the college-level difficulty criteria. The preprocessing also involved ensuring that all questions contained one or more images and were written in English.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation protocol involved a team of over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various disciplines. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The questions were categorized by subject, subfield, image type, and difficulty level. Each question was annotated with the correct answer, explanation (if available), and other relevant metadata.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotation process was managed through a user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng, which significantly improved the workflow for data curation. The interface allowed annotators to input questions, answers, and metadata in a structured format, ensuring consistency and accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process included rigorous quality control measures. A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples from the dataset were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset includes 11,550 questions, with an average of 1.02 images per question. The questions are categorized by subject, subfield, image type, and difficulty level.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators were over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in various disciplines. They were recruited from universities such as the University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, and other institutions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The dataset was curated using a combination of manual human curation and automated tools for data collection and preprocessing. Automated tools were used to identify potential duplicate problems and to standardize the format of questions and answers. However, the primary annotation process was conducted manually by a team of annotators to ensure accuracy and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The MMMU dataset is released under the MIT License. The dataset is maintained and updated by the authors, with plans to release future versions as needed. The authors have provided a version change log detailing updates and fixes to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The MMMU dataset is designed to evaluate the capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs) in the context of Expert AGI. It aims to push the boundaries of what LMMs can achieve by assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains. The dataset is intended to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases due to the manual curation process and the focus on college-level subjects. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. However, the authors believe it should be necessary for an Expert AGI system to achieve strong performance on MMMU to demonstrate their broad and deep subject knowledge as well as expert-level understanding and reasoning capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The MMMU dataset has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The dataset is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition, because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The dataset is designed to be a necessary but not sufficient criterion for an Expert AGI system.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The MMMU dataset is designed for training, testing, and evaluating large multimodal models (LMMs) on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It is intended to push the boundaries of what LMMs can achieve and stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. The dataset can be used for various purposes, including benchmarking the performance of LMMs, identifying areas for improvement, and guiding the development of next-generation models.
